leads.summary: Real hyprsunset returns six-decimal gamma values, but ownership and readback require integer strings
leads.consequence: hyprsunset v0.4.0's IPC getter uses std::to_string(float): 100.000000, 25.000000, etc. Hyprctl forwards it verbatim. With an existing neutral daemon can-dim fails, so 0% writes hardware 1% without dimming. With no daemon, a set to 25 succeeds at IPC, then ten readback comparisons fail, leaving global gamma 25 with a process PID file but no gamma ownership; active reports false and set 100 silently exits 0 without resetting it. The changed test uses an integer-only getter, hiding this. Fix by normalizing/validating numeric gamma for every equality, including can-dim, ownership, cleanup, and set verification, then test upstream-formatted replies.
leads.triage: contradicted; Opus follow-up 1: Arch hyprsunset 0.4.0-3 built with GCC 16.1.1 / CMake 4.4.0 -std=gnu++26; libstdc++ to_chars path; binary imports to_chars and no printf. Replies are shortest form. Private robustness note only.

leads.summary: Current quattro base redirects ordinary brightness keys into shell QML that cannot enter or leave the PR's gamma range
leads.consequence: A three-way merge of the PR and current quattro tip is conflict-free for media.lua: normal up/down become { brightness = 'raise'/'lower' }, while Shift+Down alone invokes the PR's 0% script. The new quattro shortcut list registers both, helpers.lua dispatches them to shell, shell.qml:1586-1588 handles internal panels with BrightnessKeys.qml rather than falling back to this script. BrightnessModel.js:1-6 clamps down at 1%, never calling gamma, and up writes only the hardware target without restoring any owned gamma. A user's default keys therefore cannot progressively dim below 1%; after Shift+Down dims with gamma, an ordinary up can increase backlight without undoing gamma. Integrate the sub-1% path with shell shortcuts or route internal keys back through the script in the merge.

leads.summary: Requesting a 1% floor is not a nonzero raw backlight floor on low-resolution devices
leads.consequence: On e.g. max_brightness=15, brightnessctl calculates roundf(1/100 * 15)=0. When current hardware is raw0, +5% selects 1%, writes raw0 and leaves current at 0; repeated up presses cannot light the screen, while OSD remains at 0. The PR's changed 0% branch similarly writes 1%, not guaranteed nonzero. A sandbox stub implementing brightnessctl's upstream percent_to_val returned raw0 twice. Related #8524 adds a raw +1 fallback for precisely this case; coordinate or use a raw floor and test max=15, not a stub that writes 1 literally.

leads.summary: Cleanup kills a brightness-owned process needed by a single user-defined nonidentity profile
leads.consequence: The guard counts profiles but assumes <=1 is safe to terminate. hyprsunset supports a single scheduled profile that sets temperature or gamma; when that custom profile is at 6500K, gamma is 100, and brightness returns to normal (or cleanup runs directly), helper kills its process and removes the ownership record, removing the user's scheduled color until restart. Sandbox owned-sleeper repro with one valid custom profile: process-alive=no, state-present=no. Default shipped one-profile identity is a different case. Distinguish stock identity from user profiles or refrain from killing when config is custom. The normal set100 route is also blocked by B1 until its numeric comparison is fixed.
